y1: The number twelve brings to mind the twelve tribes of Israel. Jesus is building God's new people. A 'disciple' (learner) now becomes an 'apostle' (sent one).
y2: The list is surprising. Matthew, who collected taxes for Rome, is together with Simon the Zealot, who fought against Rome. And at the end is Judas, who would betray Him.
y3: Zealots were people who wanted to drive Rome out by force of arms. Tax collectors collaborated with that same Rome. In Jesus, two people who were enemies became one community.
y5: Jesus first tells them to go to 'the lost sheep of the house of Israel.' Later in chapter 28, this expands to 'all nations.' God's plan has an order.
y6: The disciples are sent to do what Jesus did (preach, heal). He tells them not to put money in their belts and to stay in a house that welcomes them. 'You received freely, freely give.'
y7: When entering a house, they should wish it 'shalom' (peace). If they don't welcome it, they should shake the dust off their feet. We leave the results to God, while the disciple must faithfully proclaim.
y9: “Be wise as serpents, and innocent as doves.” Jesus does not hide that the disciples will be taken to court and hated even by their families. The Holy Spirit will give them the words to say at that time.
y10: “Don't be afraid of those who kill the body but are not able to kill the soul.” Then He gives the example of two sparrows sold for an assarion. If God remembers even a sparrow, “you are more valuable than many sparrows.”
y11: In 10:26–31, 'don't be afraid' appears three times. The secret to not fearing people is to properly fear God. A person who knows God is free before people.
y12: Acknowledging and a cup of cold water
y13: “Everyone who acknowledges me before people, I will also acknowledge before my Father in heaven.” To follow Jesus is to carry a cross.
y14: But the final words are warm. Whoever welcomes a disciple welcomes Jesus, and whoever gives one of these little ones a cup of cold water will not lose their reward. Not only great martyrdom but also small hospitality is the work of the kingdom of heaven.
y15: “Whoever finds their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life for my sake will find it” (10:39). This is the first time the word 'cross' appears in the Gospel of Matthew. Jesus Himself will go that way first.
verse: “Aren't two sparrows sold for an assarion? But not one of them falls to the ground without your Father's permission. Even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So don't be afraid, you are more valuable than many sparrows.”
prayer: Jesus, just as You called twelve ordinary and different people, made them one, and sent them out, send me out too. Let me not fear people, but fear God. Even if it's not a great work, let me live acknowledging You through kindness like a cup of cold water. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: apostle. A person who carries the authority of the one who sent them. In the Gospel of Matthew, the word 'apostle' appears only once, right here. In Azerbaijani, it is called 'həvari'.
d1: freely. Grace is not bought with money, so it should not be sold. In Acts 8, Simon is rebuked for trying to buy the power of the Holy Spirit with money.
d2: assarion. It was a very small coin. Two sparrows were sold for this price. Luke says 'five sparrows for two assarions' (Luke 12:6). God remembers even the extra sparrow thrown in.
d3: acknowledge. To say the 'same' thing before people that God says about Jesus. The opposite is to 'deny'. Peter denies Him in chapter 26.
